subject.title: Feature Request: Add channel creation to message tool

question: Should OpenClaw expose agent-driven channel creation as a default-off provider capability, and if so what opt-in, token, and provider-scope boundary is acceptable for Slack and Discord?
rationale: This is a deliberate workspace/server-administration capability, not a missing mechanical route alone; the repository policy requires explicit judgment before adding a new authority and configuration surface.

options.title: Approve a narrow provider-owned opt-in
options.body: Define default-off Slack and Discord administrative action gates, document required scopes and token behavior, and implement only the bounded creation path behind those gates.

options.title: Land only the existing Discord CLI slice
options.body: Treat the Discord CLI wiring as an independent improvement while leaving Slack channel creation and a cross-provider promise out of scope.

options.title: Decline built-in channel administration
options.body: Keep this authority outside the built-in message action surface and direct operators to provider-native automation.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow provider-owned opt-in
recommendation.body: Define default-off Slack and Discord administrative action gates, document required scopes and token behavior, and implement only the bounded creation path behind those gates.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied history and prior review place this person closest to the current message CLI and provider-action boundary.
